shortDescription: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, fell on Tuesday, pressured by weakness in the capesize vessel category.

children: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, fell on Tuesday, pressured by weakness in the capesize vessel category.
, which tracks rates for capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, fell 29 points, or 0.9%, to 3,157.
The capesize index (.BACI) was down 115 points, or 2.1%, at 5,221.
Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-ton cargoes including iron ore and coal, fell $1,049 to $43,847.

Iron ore futures were little changed, as traders weighed expectations of a pickup in port arrivals following elevated global shipments against a private survey showing accelerating factory activity in China.
The panamax index (.BPNI) gained 45 points, or 1.9%, to 2,360.
Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, increased $403 to $21,237.
Among smaller vessels, the supramax index (.BSIS) was up 3 points, or 0.18%, at 1,650.
